name: qwen3.8-flash-next-nvfp4-tp2-vllm030
description: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 on the stock vLLM 0.30.0 image: TP2 + expert parallel, MTP3, BF16 KV, 262K context. No patches, no custom image.

source.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 — stock vLLM 0.30, TP2+EP, MTP3
source.author: Mia's AI Lab (vLLM 0.30 lane, measurements), based on getrefined's TP2 recipe

measured.boot: ~11 min until the KV cache is allocated (the source's launch, weights already on both nodes)
measured.note: prose, from the source's 'v0.30 stock' column (code: 61.5 / 316.5). Measured with vLLM's default breakable CUDA graphs, which this recipe turns off: on the source's lane that made decode steadier and 13–19% faster at 2+ streams.

requirements: Image vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 (arm64, CUDA 13.0) on both nodes — Pin resolves its digest. It loads the nvidia checkpoint natively (Qwen4Exp); none of the day-0 image's patches are needed.
~126 GiB free on each node for the checkpoint (133 GB, 11 shards).
BF16 KV only: v0.30's QSA attention accepts nothing else. FP8 KV (2.64M tokens) needs a backport of vllm#55557 that the source applies as a patch; it is not part of this recipe.
notes: A port of the source's start-v030.sh (commit cd839d0b) with the same flags and environment, except its reduced draft-vocabulary overlay. That overlay drafts over 47k instead of 248k tokens and measured 5–15% faster decode (prose 57.6 / code 71.5 tok/s at one stream). It is a patch script under AGPL-3.0, so it is not included here.

gpu-memory-utilization 0.80, not higher: at 0.835 a 6-client soak left both nodes at 0.3–0.9 GiB MemAvailable, where GB10 boxes hard-reset. At 0.80 a 1-hour soak kept 4.5 GiB (node A) and 7.8 GiB (node B), with 1,348 of 1,349 requests correct.
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S 1800 is TwinSpark's addition: the source documents about 11 minutes to the KV cache allocation, close to vLLM's own 600 s limit.
FlashInfer autotunes into /tmp inside each container: a persisted cache that differed between the two nodes deadlocked TP2 at the autotune step once.
The SSM state runs in bfloat16 (the checkpoint asks for float32). This halves the state each step moves. On the source's single-Spark recipe it measured +6.8% decode at one stream and +8.5% at eight.
vLLM 0.30 fixes the missed prefix-cache hit on the first repeat of a prompt (vllm#54713, vllm#53945): multi-turn TTFT measured 0.28–0.40 s against 0.63 s on the day-0 image.
Experimental: the flags follow the published lane. Check them with `tsm plan` and the image check against the pinned image.
